catalog_quote: Le phonème /e/ se réalise: [...] - [ë] en CV accentué⁵ /pè/ [pë] «être cuit» - [ǝ] en CV non accentué⁶ /pè/ [pǝ̀] «ils» [...] ⁵ La distinction entre syllabe accentuée et syllabe non accentuée n'est pertinente que pour les variantes du phonème /e/ en syllabe CV. (p. 20) [...] 1.3. Tons. La langue kar comporte un système de trois tons: - ton bas: noté / ̀/ ou B - ton moyen: noté / ̄/ ou M - ton haut: noté / ́/ ou H. Ces trois tons ponctuels se réalisent soit sur un lexème verbal [...] soit sur un lexème nominal dans le composé épithétique,type2 [...] soit sur un morphème grammatical [...] soit sur le pronom substitutif en fonction de sujet [...] Ces tons peuvent se combiner entre eux. Il en résulte des combinaisons BM, HB et MB. Ainsi distinguons-nous cinq schèmes tonals. [...] Ces schèmes tonals sont attestés sur le mot phonologique: BB, MM, BM et HB sur les bases verbales, et BB, MM, BM, MB et HB sur les noms simples. (pp. 21-22)

(p. 20) […] 1.3. Tones. The Kar language has a system of three tones: low tone, mid tone, high tone. These three level tones are realized either on a verbal lexeme, or on a nominal lexeme in the epithetic compound, or on a grammatical morpheme. (p. 21)

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (308 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the title 'Kar Grammar-Unicode-final.doc', 2011) and its; rendered PDF pages 20-21 (printed page numbers 20 and 21 match PDF page numbers). Quote check: p. 20 reads '- [ë] en CV accentué⁵ /pè/ [pë] «être cuit» / - [ə] en CV non accentué⁶ /pè/ [pə̀] «ils»' and fn 5 'La distinction entre syllabe accentuée et syllabe non accentuée n'est pertinente que pour les variantes du phonème /e/ en syllabe CV.' (fn 6 is a typesetting duplicate of fn 5, printed '6⁵ La distinction…'). p. 21 §1.3 Tons: 'La langue kar comporte un système de trois tons: - ton bas … - ton moyen … - ton haut …' and 'Ces trois tons ponctuels se réalisent soit sur un lexème verbal … soit…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kar is a three-level-tone language (L, M, H; five tone schemes on the phonological word: BB, MM, BM, HB, MB, with object-induced tonal replacement on verbs and postpositions). The grammar's only mention of stress is that an 'accented' vs 'unaccented' CV syllable conditions /e/ allophony ([ë] vs [ə]); the examples oppose a lexical verb monosyllable (accented) to a subject pronoun (unaccented), so the contrast is content word vs. function word/clitic rather than a positional rule. No rule for where word stress falls is given in any opened source; the 1979 phonology (chapters on syllable and phonological word not in the open extract) may say more.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the footnote restricts the accented/unaccented distinction to /e/ in CV syllables only.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexeme vs grammatical morpheme; 'mot phonologique'); the phonology chapter is a summary ('rappel') of Wichser & Bühler 1979, whose full text (78 pp; HathiTrust search-only, htid uva.x001635739) could not be opened. Dictionary (Sagnon & Wichser 2012) marks base tones of citation forms and notes heavy tonal variation on verbs and pronouns, nothing on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All first-hand sources describe the kar dialect of Tiéfora, the eastern Karaboro group (self-name Kai, language kar) = east2398 exactly. The western group (Syer/Tenyer, Tengrela) is a separate language, west2466 (Dombrowsky-Hahn 2015; Prost 1964); Wichser 1994 p. 6 says 'Sauf indication contraire, nous nous référerons uniquement au parler du groupe de l'est'. The earlier scan's 'Mills 1984' pointer is a misattribution: Mills 1984 is a phonology of Ivorian Senari (Cebaara) and Glottolog cites only its pp. xii-xx (classification) for Kar.

sources.note: Second-hand (SIL 2009 via Roberts): Karaboro has grammatical tone marking number - noun plurals that carry no segmental plural marker are distinguished from the singular by tone and all end in a low tone, which the orthography writes with a word-final hyphen; tone-marked pairs kāī 'affair' / kāì 'affairs', sààpjé 'rabbit' / sàápjè 'rabbits' (H, M, L marks); p. 105 cites Karaboro as the counterexample to the tendency for tonal plurals to be higher-toned than singulars. A passing example in a survey of tone orthographies, not a description of the Kar tone system.

tone.quote: For example, Karaboro (Gur, Burkina Faso; SIL 2009) adds a hyphen to plurals that have no segmental marker to distinguish them from their singular counterparts (examples 10 - 17). Since these consistently end in L tone, the hyphen can be taught as either representing meaning or sound in this particular context: 10 <dyɛ> [dʲɛ̀] year 11 <dʲɛ-> [dʲɛ̂] years 12 <kai> [kāī] affair 13 <kai-> [kāì] affairs 14 <jɔɔ> [gʲɔ̀ɔ́] net 15 <jɔɔ-> [gʲɔ́ɔ̀] nets 16 <saapye> [sààpʲé] rabbit 17 <saapye-> [sàápʲè] rabbits
